title: Graph-compatible B70 doorbells and command-streamer alternatives

assumptions: The two-lane doorbell domain stands for independently owned physical-card lanes; production cardinality and layer count are not inferred from the finite model.
A staged tensor payload is abstracted to an ordering state. Numerical MoE correctness, buffer extents and dtype conversion are specified by provider/compute branches.
The model treats CUDA Driver and Runtime operations as successfully enqueued. stream_signal.py does not check their return codes, so API refusal remains an external implementation failure.
Classic providerSequence is poller-owned call identity only. The signal value is exactly zero or M and completion is exactly zero or one; neither flag carries a sequence.
Completion releases an untimed CUDA waiter but does not imply valid output. Validity and cumulative error observation are independent state.
Captured replay has no Python error check; the first later eager forward can observe errors after stale data was copied.
One native poller/provider/queue owns one physical B70, and caller-owned flags and staging buffers remain alive until poller destruction.
Command-streamer selection is independent of CUDA graph enablement; the current r15 recipe selects graph-compatible signaling with classic native polling because CS_DOORBELL is unset.
The command-streamer model's two layers represent the implementation guard known == total_layers and all-step ordering, not a claim that a bank has two layers.
Chain and ride are eligible only after arming, complete registration, NVFP4-compatible provider state and M at most 32; larger work remains classic.
Baked mode additionally requires M equal to one and FP16 output, and a busy bounded wait is recoverable while monotone per-list progress continues.
After baked recovery only signals whose completions prove consumption may be scrubbed; an unconsumed racing signal must survive for classic fallback.
Host registration and CPU affinity failures are performance degradations according to source, not modeled correctness failures.
No fairness, latency, driver cache-coherence, queue-clock comparability or hardware progress property is claimed.

implementation_checks.description: CPU source-order inspection: verify issue status gates take, error accounting precedes the unconditional sequentially-consistent fence and completion[0]=1 store, and signal is cleared before classic issue. This compares ordering only, not hardware visibility.

CPU AST/source inspection: verify wait_flag(completion,1) precedes result H2D/cast and write_flag(completion,0) follows both; compare forward_modular's error_count read to document the later eager observation boundary.

CPU ABI correspondence scan: compare header declarations, b70_capi.cpp extern-C definitions and b70_binding.py ctypes lookups; report the implementation/binding symbol sb_b70_poll_arm_cs as absent from the public header rather than silently accepting drift.
Potential CPU execution checks only placement partition, count, capability, threshold and global-ID/compact-slot prerequisites. Record it explicitly as non-doorbell evidence.

Hardware-only differential: on available CUDA, compare eager and graph-replay exact-equality blocking, release on host value 1, and consumption of a fresh signal on the second replay. This is not a CPU implementation comparison.

CPU source inspection: verify progress is monotone per layer within a submitted step, reset before submission, written after completion in each baked list, and used instead of sampled completion counts during bounded recovery.
